questions.question: Explain Wumpus World problem in detail.
questions.solution_html:
• The Wumpus computer game, The agent explores a cave consisting of rooms
  • connected by passageways, somewhere in the cave is the Wumpus, a beast
  • that eats any agent that enters its room. Some rooms contain bottomless pits
  • that trap any agent that wanders into the room. The Wumpus can fall into a pit
  • too, so avoids them. Occasionally, there is a heap of gold in a room.The goal
  • is to collect the gold and exit the world without being eaten.
  • Major terms: Pits: breeze, Wumpus, stench, arrow
  • PEAS: Performance measures: ( Agent gets gold and return back safe
  • = +1000 points, Agent dies (pit or Wumpus)= -1000 points, Each move of the
  • agent = -1 point, Agent uses the arrow = -10 points) Environment:( A cave
  • with 16(4x4) rooms)Actuators: (Move forward,,Turn right/left: Rotate Shoot
  • Grab, Drop)Sensors: (Breeze,Stench, Glitter,Scream,Bump)
  • Mark Distribution: Major terms((2 marks)), PEAS description((2 marks)), General
  • overview of the game with or without figure( (2 marks))
  • Episodic(next episode is independent) vs sequential(current episode
  • determines next episode)
questions.final_answer: determines next episode)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Examine and interpret the roles of selection, crossover, and mutation in Genetic Algorithms in achieving evolutionary optimization.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine and interpret the roles of selection, crossover, and mutation in
  • Genetic Algorithms in achieving evolutionary optimization.
  • Basic terms: selection, crossover, and mutation.
  • Selection- Selecting the individual solutions based on fitness function.
  • Crossover combines genetic information from two parent individuals to
  • produce offspring.
  • Mutation randomly alters one or more genes in an individual.Prevents the
  • algorithm from getting stuck in local optima.
  • Mark Distribution: Basic idea of GA((2 marks)), Major terms((2 marks)), diagram
  • or example((2 marks))
questions.final_answer: or example()
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: List the differences between forward chaining and backward chaining.
questions.solution_html:
• List the differences between forward chaining and backward chaining.
  • Forward chaining is a data-driven approach that starts with known facts and
  • applies IF–THEN rules to generate new facts until a goal is reached; it moves
  • step by step from available information toward conclusions.
  • In backward chaining is a goal-driven approach that starts with a desired goal
  • and works backward by checking which rules could produce that goal, then
  • verifying whether their conditions are true (or can be proven).
  • Mark distribution : Forward chaining with diagram or example- (2 marks), Backward
  • chaining with diagram or example-(2 marks), Difference- (2 marks)
questions.final_answer: chaining with diagram or example-, Difference
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the concept of unsupervised learning.
questions.solution_html:
• Unsupervised learning is a type of machine learning where a model learns
  • patterns and structures from unlabeled data. The system must discover hidden
  • relationships on its own.
  • Key terms/ characteristics- unlabeled dataset, pattern discovery, exploratory
  • data analysis, eg: clustering.
  • Applications: image pattern recognition, anomaly detection, customer
  • segmentation
  • Mark Distribution: Major concept of unsupervised learning- (3 marks)
  • example- (1 mark), applications- (2 marks)
  • Essay Questions
  • Describe MIN-MAX algorithm in detail with its principle, algorithm and
